Sibling of dispatch-policy.json, which covers the CI dispatch path. This one covers the
agent containers: the ones whose sops secrets declare GH_TOKEN and which mount the shared
Measured 2026-09-24 from inside my-ai_claude-api (dispatched slot 467), value never printed:
GH_TOKEN is SET (len 40, ghp_ classic PAT) and `gh auth status` reports it as the source.
With GH_TOKEN unset, gh is logged out (no ~/.config/gh). So the claim that GH_TOKEN is EMPTY
in the claude container while gh stays authenticated is WRONG for this container. It
matches HERMES: hermes strips GH_TOKEN from its tool shells, and _dispatch/creds.sh puts it
back on disk (~/.config/gh/hosts.yml + ~/.git-credentials) so those shells can push. Either
way the agent holds the full token. The blast radius is not smaller than recorded.
Checked by 9_others/test/test_agent_credential_scope.sh, which reads THIS file.
Measure a live token with 9_others/src/agent-credential-audit.sh (exit 1 = over-scoped).
_holders_comment: cloud-u-containers service dirs whose src/secrets.yaml declares the env_var key. The tester
works this out from the sops files (key names are plaintext) and fails if it differs from
this list. A new container that picks up the agent token must be added here on purpose.

plaintext_copies_found: /home/appuser/.git-credentials in my-ai_claude-api: 0600, same value as GH_TOKEN, written 2026-09-24 17:37 UTC. /home/appuser is a host bind mount, so the copy outlives the container.

Cause: credential.helper=store in the SHARED tree's repo-local .git/config (cloud-data, cloud-data-my-ai-memory, cloud-infra, cloud-u-android, cloud-u-containers, cloud-u-linux; set 2026-09-17, no declared source). Git passes every credential that works to EVERY configured helper, so any fetch or push by any agent writes the token into that container's $HOME.

what_an_agent_needs.action: clone, fetch, commit and push to main
push commits that touch .github/workflows/* (23 agent commits in cloud-infra since 2026-09-10)
watch its own CI: gh run list/view, job logs

_allowed_classic_scopes_comment: The fallback if a fine-grained token is not possible. The audit reports every scope the live
token has beyond these as excess and exits 1. Target is fine-grained: classic `repo` still
covers EVERY repo on the account.

repository_access._comment: The repos agents clone ARE the repos the token needs. Taken from runtime.repos so the list cannot drift from the container's bootstrap list. Open decision for Diego: runtime.repos includes cloud-vault (key material). A fine-grained token has the same permissions on every selected repo, so leaving cloud-vault in grants agents WRITE to it. Recommendation: remove cloud-vault from the agent token, and from runtime.repos if agents do not need it.
repository_access.plus_submodules_of: entries with submodules:true are cloned --recurse-submodules through the same credential helper (start.sh rewrites SSH to HTTPS), so their .gitmodules repos must be selected too. 2026-09-24: cloud-infra -> diegonmarcos/cloud (I_cloud). Leave it out and the bootstrap leaves a_solutions empty after the mint.

explicitly_not_granted: Any organization or enterprise permission (classic admin:org, admin:enterprise, audit_log).
Packages: GHCR writes are done by CI, not agents (classic write:packages, delete:packages).
Account-level: user, gist, codespace, copilot, admin:*_key, notifications, project.
diego_must_do: 1. github.com > avatar > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens > Generate new token.
2. Token name 'agent-push-359'. Resource owner: diegonmarcos. Expiration: 90 days.
3. Repository access: 'Only select repositories'. Tick every repo in repository_access (jq it from runtime.repos; decide on cloud-vault first) plus the plus_submodules_of repos.

4. Repository permissions: Contents = Read and write. Workflows = Read and write. Actions = Read-only. Metadata = Read-only (set automatically). Leave every other repository permission and ALL account permissions at 'No access'. Generate token.
5. Put it in each holder's src/secrets.yaml under GH_TOKEN with `sops` (same key name, so no code change): cloud-u-containers/<holder>/src/secrets.yaml for every holder above. Commit.

6. At a quiet time (no agent running), ship the three holders. Shipping recreates them and ends any agent inside. The my-ai-api ship also deploys the #359 bots split (cloud-agi-bots loses GH_TOKEN, /run/secrets and the tree), which is committed but undeployed on purpose.
7. Actions > lint-agent-credential > Run workflow. Expect green: every holder 'fine-grained token'. It is RED until this is done.
8. Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Tokens (classic): delete the old token that had admin:enterprise. Keep a classic token only where a human uses it, never in a container.

services_that_hold_it._comment: #359. Inside a holder's compose project, only build.json agent.services get the token, the /run/secrets mounts and the writable tree. Every other service keeps the .secrets env_file with GH_TOKEN blanked (compose: environment beats env_file). Declared per container, decided by cloud-u-containers/_shared/agent-credential.nix, tested by _shared/test-agent-credential-scope.mjs (per-service-tests).
withheld_2026_09_24: user-ai_my-ai-api/cloud-agi-bots: the Telegram gateway (#542). Only HTTP calls, no git, no gh, never reads /run/secrets. It held the full PAT three ways plus a push helper.
agents_that_keep_it: user-ai_hermes-agent/hermes-agent (one service: the Telegram gateway and the agent are the same process)

dispatch_path_scoping: Asked (#359): give GH_TOKEN only to the dispatch path, not the whole container. Compose cannot do that, and nothing inside the container would enforce it.

env_file and environment apply to the whole container. A dispatched agent is `docker exec` into that same container as uid 10001, the same uid as the Node front, the Headroom sidecar and every `claude -p` the front spawns for other callers. That uid can read /proc/1/environ and /run/secrets/GH_TOKEN whatever the exec itself was given.

Moving the token to a file only the exec reads, or stripping it from the front's children, would stop accidents and not an agent: anything that can push can read the token. The container is the smallest unit compose can scope, so #359 scopes at the service level (services_that_hold_it). The token's own scope (diego_must_do) is the real limit.
guard: lint-agent-credential.yml runs 9_others/src/agent-credential-declared-guard.sh daily and on policy/guard pushes: it sops-decrypts each holder's declared GH_TOKEN and runs agent-credential-audit.sh on it (GET /user, X-OAuth-Scopes, token never printed). Exit 1 if any holder's token has a scope outside allowed_classic_scopes; admin:enterprise is one of them. Its logic is proven offline by test_agent_credential_scope.sh case I.
container_side_now: Removed credential.helper=store from the shared tree's repo-local configs and deleted the stray ~/.git-credentials in my-ai_claude-api (2026-09-24, #439). No auth path depended on either: claude-api and my-ai-api authenticate through the engine's env credential helper, and hermes through its own global store helper written by creds.sh. The audit reports both if they come back.

Nothing else is possible without a new token. The agent runs as the same uid that holds the credential (env, /proc/self/environ, creds.sh files), so anything that can push can read the token and use every scope it has. A gh wrapper or a Claude deny rule would only stop accidents; curl with the token gets around either. The token's own scope is the only real limit.
